Are you looking for the best mobile app development teams in Miami, Florida? You’re in the right place. Known for its mix of culture, commerce, and creativity, Miami has quickly become one of the fastest-growing tech hubs in the U.S. The city’s developer community combines expertise in mobile engineering with strong ties to industries like fintech, healthcare, logistics, and tourism—sectors that thrive in the Miami metro region.
This guide will share practical tips on how to find the most suitable mobile app developers in Miami. We’ve curated a list of agencies that stand out for their technical skills, design excellence, and proven track records, helping you connect with the right partner for your next project.
Miami’s app developers cover the full spectrum of services—product strategy, UX research, UI design, native and cross-platform coding, QA, and post-launch optimization. Many also provide growth-oriented services such as app marketing, analytics integration, and monetization consulting. Whether you’re a startup seeking an MVP or an enterprise building a large-scale platform, Miami developers are equipped to deliver.
For each company in our list, we include key details such as year founded, team size, revenue estimates, social presence, and monthly website traffic. This allows you to assess not just the portfolio but also the business credibility of each agency.
- Advertisement -

## The app developer market in Miami
Miami’s rise as a technology hub has been accelerated by the influx of entrepreneurs, investors, and companies relocating from other U.S. cities. With its geographic position, Miami also serves as a gateway to Latin America, giving local developers valuable exposure to bilingual and multicultural markets.
App development agencies in Miami create award-winning iOS and Android apps for startups, corporates, and government bodies. These app developers offer end-to-end solutions, often extending into cloud infrastructure, IoT, and AI-driven applications.
Notable companies in Miami include **TECKpert**, which focuses on technology consulting and custom app development; **SDSOL Technologies**, a global software development firm with a strong Miami presence; **Koombea**, known for agile development and user-centric design; and **Furation Tech Solutions**, which delivers full-stack mobile and web platforms. Together, they represent the breadth of talent available in the Miami market.
**_Miami app developer example_**
_Source: Koombea_

## The best Miami app developers
### **Chop Dawg**
Chop Dawgis an award-winning web and mobile app agency. For over 17 years, they have helped entrepreneurs, startups, growing businesses, Fortune 500s, nonprofits, and government agencies transform bold ideas into scalable, profitable apps and custom software. More than just an app development company, Chop Dawg becomes your dedicated team, handling every aspect of your app so you can focus on running your business.
**Overview**
Since 2009, Chop Dawg has launched over 500 apps that have impacted more than a billion users worldwide. Their 92% client retention rate speaks to the long-term partnerships they build, with most partners continuing to work with them for years beyond their initial project. The team operates across the United States, Brazil, and Pakistan, offering flexible options to balance cost savings without sacrificing quality.
Chop Dawg has earned recognition from Inc. 5000, Clutch, Forbes, Fast Company, TechCrunch, The New York Times, and NBC, and has supported organizations including NASA, The White House, the U.S. Navy, University of Pennsylvania, Hilton, Siemens, Wawa, Six Flags, and Mister Softee. Their apps have ranked in the Top 10 on both the Apple App Store and Google Play Store within 24 hours of launch.
What sets Chop Dawg apart is their proven process and unwavering commitment to transparency. Every project includes a dedicated project manager, daily Slack communication, weekly Zoom meetings, and comprehensive documentation that future-proofs your success. From complimentary 45-minute consultations to fixed-monthly-rate pricing with clear timelines, you always know exactly what to expect.
**Services**
*   Chop Dawg provides its customers with the following services:  
*   Designing and building custom mobile apps for iOS, Android, tablets, wearables, CarPlay, and Android Auto  
*   Developing scalable web applications, eCommerce platforms, WordPress sites, and enterprise software  
*   Creating user-centric UI/UX designs, wireframes, high-fidelity prototypes, and complete branding assets  
*   Building AI-powered solutions, blockchain applications, smart contracts, and AR/VR experiences  
*   Providing ongoing maintenance, support, DevOps services, and long-term partnership for continuous growth

## Why work with an app developer based in Miami?
Miami app developers bring a unique blend of U.S. technical standards and international business perspective. Their expertise extends across fintech, healthcare, e-commerce, hospitality, and logistics—industries where Miami has global influence.
Many Miami firms are deeply collaborative, working closely with clients through discovery workshops, rapid prototyping, and iterative sprints. This ensures solutions align not just with technical requirements but also with user behavior and market positioning.
Common areas of specialization include:
*   **Smart coding:** Expertise in Swift, Kotlin, React Native, Flutter, and modern back-end frameworks.  
*   **UI design:** Clean, user-friendly interfaces optimized for conversion and engagement.  
*   **UX research:** Data-driven insights to guide feature prioritization and usability improvements.  
*   **Software development:** End-to-end builds for iOS, Android, cross-platform, and hybrid solutions.  
*   **Post-launch support:** Ongoing QA, updates, and scaling assistance to keep apps competitive.
**_Miami app developer example_**
_Source: TECKpert_

## How much does hiring Miami app developers cost?
The average salary of a mobile developer in Miami is:
| Role | Average Salary | Typical Range (25th–75th Percentile) |  
| --- | --- | --- |  
| Mobile Developer | $93k / year | $72k – $118k |  
| iOS Developer | $96k / year | $77k – $123k |  
| Android Developer | $97k / year | $75k – $125k |
_Data source: Glassdoor_
Project costs will depend on factors such as:
*   **Developer experience:** Senior engineers and architects cost more but bring efficiency and reliability.  
*   **App complexity:** Features like AI, machine learning, or AR/VR raise project scope and cost.  
*   **Customization:** Tailored solutions require more design and coding hours.  
*   **Timeline:** Faster turnarounds often demand additional resources.
Agencies in Miami typically bill between $100–$175 per hour. While this is higher than global outsourcing destinations, Miami firms bring the advantage of U.S. standards, time-zone alignment, and cultural fit for North American clients.

## How to choose the top Miami app developers
Selecting the right Miami app developer comes down to more than just price. Consider these factors:

## How to choose the top Miami app developers
### Check the portfolio
Look for examples in your industry. **Koombea** highlights strong design-led builds, while **SDSOL Technologies** demonstrates capacity for enterprise-scale platforms.

## How to choose the top Miami app developers
### Review client references
Ask for testimonials and case studies. Reliable agencies will connect you with previous clients who can vouch for communication, delivery, and support.

## How to choose the top Miami app developers
### Previous client priorities
Some Miami firms specialize in startup MVPs, while others work primarily with enterprises. Match their strengths to your business stage.

## How to choose the top Miami app developers
### Future app support
Ensure your chosen developer provides long-term maintenance, including OS updates, bug fixes, and performance improvements.

## How to choose the top Miami app developers
### Cost
Balance cost with track record. Higher hourly rates may bring more efficiency and lower risk in the long run.

## How to choose the top Miami app developers
### App delivery time
Confirm project timelines upfront and check whether agile delivery models are used to ensure steady progress.
**_Miami app developer example_**
_Source: SDSOL Technologies_

## Top mobile app development companies in Miami
You’ve seen how Miami is rapidly becoming a go-to destination for mobile app development. Now it’s time to explore the companies that stand out.
Working with a Miami app developer gives you access to skilled engineers, strong design culture, and bilingual talent pools that make products more inclusive.
Other advantages include:
*   Expertise across iOS, Android, hybrid, and cross-platform frameworks  
*   Experience serving fintech, healthcare, tourism, logistics, and retail clients  
*   Integration of marketing and analytics alongside development  
*   Competitive costs compared to larger U.S. tech hubs like New York and San Francisco  
*   Access to multicultural and bilingual teams that add value to user research and design
Here we’ve curated the best Miami app developers, blending a range of budgets, specialties, and industries to help you find the right partner for your app project.

He set a goal of $50,000 in sales for the first three months. He did $14 million.
Sixteen years later, his company was doing more than $10 billion a year. Then the founder of SoftBank handed him a struggling U.S. carrier that was bleeding customers and billions of dollars, and told him to fix it. He had never run a carrier in his life.
His name is Marcelo Claure. And the reason he kept getting handed impossible jobs is the same reason most people never get them: people bet on operators, not resumes.
Claure was born in 1970 in Guatemala City. His father was a Bolivian who worked for the United Nations, so the family moved constantly. Morocco as an infant. The Dominican Republic as a kid. Then high school in La Paz, Bolivia.
He left Bolivia in 1989 for college in Massachusetts. At Bentley College, he started a business buying and selling airline frequent flyer miles. He had 25 people working for him within a year. Airlines told him it was illegal. He found a legal way to do it.

# Connor Gillivan - He set a goal of $50,000 in sales for... | Facebook
## Connor Gillivan's Post
After graduation, a chance meeting changed his trajectory. On a flight, he got talking with a leader of Bolivia's football federation, who hired him to run the team's business operations. Bolivia qualified for the 1994 World Cup, its first qualification in 44 years.
Back in Boston, a cell phone shop owner who was fed up with retail offered Claure the business. Within two years, he owned 150 stores across the Northeast and had built one of the region's leading wireless retailers.
In October 1997, Claure and partner Dave Peterson founded Brightstar in Miami. They sold everything they had, borrowed more, and launched the company. The idea: help phone manufacturers get handsets to Latin American carriers, handling customs and logistics nobody else wanted to touch.
Their goal for the first three months was $50,000 in sales. They did $14 million. $73 million in year two. $355 million in year three.
By 2002, Brightstar was the top distributor in every country where it operated. By 2013, it had about $10.5 billion in gross revenue, operations in roughly 50 countries, and the top spot on the HispanicBusiness 500 list of the largest Hispanic-owned companies in the US, five of the past six years.
In October 2013, SoftBank agreed to buy a majority stake in Brightstar for $1.26 billion.
Then Masayoshi Son made a bigger bet on Claure himself.
In August 2014, Son chose Claure to become President and CEO of Sprint. SoftBank had paid $21.6 billion for control of Sprint in 2013. The company was losing customers and losing money. In his first fiscal year as CEO, Sprint lost $3.3 billion. The industry was skeptical. Claure had never operated a telecom network. His background was wireless distribution, not running a carrier.
He turned it around anyway. Sprint went from losing customers to adding more than 2.1 million. In fiscal 2017, it posted its highest operating income in company history and its first annual net income in 11 years.

# Connor Gillivan - He set a goal of $50,000 in sales for... | Facebook
## Connor Gillivan's Post
In 2018, Son moved him again. Claure became Executive Chairman of Sprint, COO of SoftBank Group and CEO of SoftBank Group International, overseeing a portfolio that included Arm and Fortress. He kept pushing the Sprint and T-Mobile merger through a long regulatory fight, and it closed in April 2020. Today he's T-Mobile's largest independent shareholder.
At SoftBank, he also noticed a gap almost nobody was talking about: Latin American startups were getting a sliver of the venture money flowing to China and India. SoftBank launched a dedicated Latin America innovation fund to go after it.
After the George Floyd protests in 2020, Claure went to Son about doing something real. SoftBank put together a $100 million Opportunity Growth Fund for founders of color in about 24 hours.
Today Claure runs Claure Group, his own investment firm. He is Group Vice Chairman of Shein. He launched Bicycle Capital, a Latin America-focused growth fund. He owns Club Bolívar, co-owns Girona FC, and bought 10% of New York City FC. Bloomberg has estimated his net worth at about $2 billion, making him Bolivia's wealthiest person.
From a dorm-room frequent flyer business to running a carrier SoftBank paid $21.6 billion for. Built by a man who kept getting impossible jobs because the people handing them out weren't betting on his resume. They were betting on the operator.
Here's what I take from Marcelo Claure.
SoftBank didn't just buy a distribution business. It got the person running it. Then it handed him Sprint, a carrier losing billions, because it trusted the operator more than any domain expertise.
That's what I've learned across the portfolio. The partnerships that work, the clients that stay, the opportunities that open up, none of them come because of a specific credential. They come because people trust how you operate. They've seen you handle complexity, make decisions under pressure, and deliver results in one context, and they bet you can do it in another.
Nobody hires an operator for what they know about one industry. They hire an operator for how they think across all of them.

Victoire Cogevina, the CEO and co-founder of Gloria, a social media app for soccer players and fans alike, has lived in 11 cities throughout the world, and with each move, she used her fandom for soccer as a way to make new friends and find her tribe. Her dad was a Greek ambassador, and her mother Argentinian. Cogevina was born in Boston.
“Football was a vehicle to connect with the different places I lived. I made friends that way,” she said. “Football” is what the rest of the world calls “soccer.”
Cogevina founded Gloria in Miami in 2018 but soon left for San Francisco looking for a co-founder and CTO and also chasing investment dollars. Gloria – now in beta – is slated to make a soft launch this year and the full launch is scheduled for the 2022 World Cup in Qatar.
“I met my first angel investor at the World Cup and he convinced me that I would find my business partner and investors in San Francisco,” she said. Turns out he was right.
Cogevina, who recently moved back to Miami, citing it as – “the best American city for football” met Matias Castello, a fellow Argentine soccer fan and previously a product guy at Facebook. “I moved two blocks from him” and over a 6-month period, she said, she convinced him to join her as her co-founder and CTO at Gloria.
“The reason why I moved here [Miami] now is because the future of football in the U.S. is in Miami. The highest broadcasting rates come from here. Since I’m the one in charge of selling the product, I can’t be in San Francisco where football isn’t really a thing,” Cogevina said. Castello (pictured above) continues to be based in San Francisco, and the rest of the company is remote. The team of 6, which include the two co-founders and four engineers, is looking to grow. They’ll be adding more engineers to the team as well as people on the sales and marketing side.
The company plans to make money by charging a subscription rate.
texts.1:
While Cogevina doesn’t play soccer herself – “I play golf,” she said – for her, soccer has been more than a fun way to meet people. It’s played a large role in her career thus far. In Miami, in 2015, she and her mother founded SR All Stars, a Miami-based soccer agency representing elite LATAM professional players in the MLS. It’s the first soccer agency in the world to be started and managed solely by women, she said. Her mother still runs the agency today.
“I grew up in countries where women didn’t play soccer. So it’s great to be in the U.S. where soccer is a women’s’ sport and not a men’s’ sport,” said Cogevina, who lived largely in Europe and Latin America growing up.
As a woman who doesn’t play soccer, yet has largely worked in it, she said her mother taught her to never think of herself as a woman first, but rather just as a person.
“We forget now, because women are in fashion these days, but we forget that women weren’t allowed to play [soccer],” she said. “Whenever I brought up being a woman, she [her mom] would look at me and say ‘Why are you bringing that up? Just focus on who you are and be the best that you can be, and that’s all that matters,’” Cogevina said.
Indeed, her mother was a wealth manager who helped a lot of soccer players manage their money, and over time she found herself helping them manage their careers, too. That’s how the mother-daughter duo broke into the business of soccer.
Today, while building her app – which has received investment from Initialized Capital and Muse Capital, and has Alexis Ohanian on the board – Cogevina is also a United Nations ambassador for gender equality in soccer. Additionally, she is on the board of Women in Sports Tech (WiST), the “leading organization to drive growth opportunities for women in the fast-growing sports tech industry,” according to the organization’s website. “50% of the U.S. labor force, sports fans, and athletes are women – and yet the representation of women in sports tech is a small fraction of that,” says WiST, which aims to change that.
texts.2:
Cogevina never considered her gender when she had the idea for Gloria, but she remembers meeting other women who thought it was a little odd that a woman was building “the home of football online,” she said. “My mom never ever let me use my gender as an excuse to not do something,” she said.
Gloria – which I got a preview of – allows players (from amateur to professional) to upload videos of themselves playing, and it has a newly created Communities section, “which has a lot of similarities to Reddit, so it’s been amazing to have someone like Alexis guide us,” Cogevina added. Gloria recently closed a seed round for an undisclosed amount and with undisclosed investors.

Spencer Rascoff
Spencer Rascoff serves as executive chairman of dot.LA. Prior to Zillow, Spencer co-founded and was VP Corporate Development of Hotwire, which was sold to Expedia for $685 million in 2003. Through his startup studio and venture capital firm, 75 & Sunny, Spencer is an active angel investor in over 100 companies and is incubating several more.
Image from Wikipedia Commons
On this episode of the Office Hours podcast, host Spencer Rascoff talks with Mayor Suarez about his vision for building a tech hub in Miami and how the pandemic and changes in work culture helped it gain momentum.
Francis Suarez grew up around city government. His father, Xavier, was mayor of the city from 1985 to 1993. After earning a bachelors in finance and a law degree from the University of Florida, the younger Suarez followed in his dad’s footsteps, becoming the first Miami-born mayor in 2017.
* * *
He quickly set out to entice more businesses to the city.
“We had great weather, we had a great tax environment, you know, we were a very international city, those were things that were always present,” he said. “What we missed, or what we were lacking was a critical mass of doers that could make deals happen,” said Suarez.
The disruption that COVID brought to workplaces helped hasten Miami’s development, Suarez said, but he credits policies–including Florida’s reopening sooner than most other states after COVID lockdowns, lower taxes and his own efforts to “roll out the red carpet” to entrepreneurs–that made Miami a central destination for tech workers.

“We wanted to create sort of a c-suite concierge service for people who want it to build our economy and the KPIs on that are we're number one in the nation and tech job growth since then,” he said, adding that he thought the pandemic accelerated Miami’s transformation into tech hub, squeezing 20 years of growth into 24 months. “So I think our efforts have been successful at trying to create prosperity for our citizens.”
One of Suarez’s most interesting accomplishments has been creating a cryptocurrency specific to his city, MiamiCoin. He said he took to crypto early as a way to bring transparency and trust to the government.
“We don't trust our politicians, we don't trust their decisions. We don't trust, you know, the media,” he said. “So how do you restore that trust? You do it in a way or you design something that you can't manipulate,” said Suarez.
He said he hopes to overtake San Francisco as the VC capital of the world in the next two years.
Key to that effort, the lifelong Republican said, will be an approach that doesn’t try to shame entrepreneurs for their successes, something he said rival cities have done.
“I hear a lot of people say, ‘You know, I didn't move [to Miami] because of the taxes. I've moved, because I didn't feel wanted in the place where I live. I felt like I was a pariah. And I've come here and people want me to [...] create high-paying jobs so that there isn't a guilt associated with success’,” said Suarez.
That, he said, requires humility on the part of government officials and an understanding that the government can’t solve all of society's problems.
”There are things that we can do to create more fairness,” he said. “Then we have to let the private sector, the NGOs, the religious organizations and society generally all come together as a community with a moral purpose, to try to make our world better.”

**Happy Friday, Los Angeles.**
Southern California’s defense-tech industry has spent the past several years looking toward the sky.
Odin Dynamics is heading in the opposite direction.
The Los Angeles startup emerged from stealth this week with $17M in total funding to build autonomous vessels designed to operate above and below the ocean’s surface.
The financing includes a $13.75M seed round from Freestyle VC, BlueYard Capital and Sierra Ventures.
Its first product is Dolphin, a family of unmanned underwater vehicles built for long-range naval missions. The smaller Dolphin S can operate for more than three days, carry roughly 50 pounds and be deployed without the submarines and other expensive infrastructure required by conventional torpedoes.
The company is also developing a medium-sized version capable of carrying significantly larger payloads, along with an autonomous surface vessel and a separate line of power systems for the Navy.
This is not merely a prototype looking for a customer. Odin says it secured more than $20M in contracts during its first year, and its Dolphin platform is already covered by a Pentagon prototype agreement. The company expects to begin delivering Dolphin S vehicles to the Navy in early 2027.
That speed reflects a broader shift in how the Pentagon is approaching military technology. Instead of relying exclusively on a small number of large and costly platforms, defense agencies are increasingly looking for autonomous systems that can be manufactured quickly, deployed in greater numbers and adapted for multiple missions.
For undersea operations, the engineering challenge is especially difficult. Vehicles must navigate without dependable GPS or communications, withstand pressure and remain operational for days without human intervention.
Odin’s answer begins with energy.
Co-founder and CEO Amir Hasan Khan previously worked on batteries and powertrains at Tesla before helping develop electric boats at Arc. Odin now designs its batteries and powertrains internally, combining them with its autonomy software to extend the range and endurance of its vessels.
That vertical approach is increasingly familiar across Southern California’s defense sector. Companies such as Anduril, Castelion, Mach Industries and Neros are building more of their hardware, software and manufacturing systems under one roof, aiming to move from concept to deployment faster than traditional procurement cycles typically allow.
Odin is applying that same philosophy to a part of the defense market that receives far less public attention than drones, missiles or satellites.

## 🔦 Spotlight
The ocean may be less visible, but it is becoming increasingly important. Undersea cables carry global communications, maritime routes underpin international trade and the Indo-Pacific has placed naval technology closer to the center of U.S. defense planning.
Odin is positioning itself for that change with systems designed to travel farther, remain at sea longer and be produced at a scale that conventional naval hardware rarely reaches.
The company still has to prove it can turn early contracts and working prototypes into reliable production. But it is already moving beyond the stage where many hardware startups stall: building a compelling demonstration without securing a path to deployment.
Los Angeles’ defense-tech ecosystem has become known for rockets, aircraft and autonomous systems in the sky. Odin’s arrival suggests its next frontier may be the one beneath the surface.

He set a goal of $50,000 in sales for the first three months. He did $14 million.
Sixteen years later, his company was doing more than $10 billion a year. Then the founder of SoftBank handed him a struggling U.S. carrier that was bleeding customers and billions of dollars, and told him to fix it. He had never run a carrier in his life.
His name is Marcelo Claure. And the reason he kept getting handed impossible jobs is the same reason most people never get them: people bet on operators, not resumes.
Claure was born in 1970 in Guatemala City. His father was a Bolivian who worked for the United Nations, so the family moved constantly. Morocco as an infant. The Dominican Republic as a kid. Then high school in La Paz, Bolivia.
He left Bolivia in 1989 for college in Massachusetts. At Bentley College, he started a business buying and selling airline frequent flyer miles. He had 25 people working for him within a year. Airlines told him it was illegal. He found a legal way to do it.

After graduation, a chance meeting changed his trajectory. On a flight, he got talking with a leader of Bolivia's football federation, who hired him to run the team's business operations. Bolivia qualified for the 1994 World Cup, its first qualification in 44 years.
Back in Boston, a cell phone shop owner who was fed up with retail offered Claure the business. Within two years, he owned 150 stores across the Northeast and had built one of the region's leading wireless retailers.
In October 1997, Claure and partner Dave Peterson founded Brightstar in Miami. They sold everything they had, borrowed more, and launched the company. The idea: help phone manufacturers get handsets to Latin American carriers, handling customs and logistics nobody else wanted to touch.
Their goal for the first three months was $50,000 in sales. They did $14 million. $73 million in year two. $355 million in year three.
By 2002, Brightstar was the top distributor in every country where it operated. By 2013, it had about $10.5 billion in gross revenue, operations in roughly 50 countries, and the top spot on the HispanicBusiness 500 list of the largest Hispanic-owned companies in the US, five of the past six years.
In October 2013, SoftBank agreed to buy a majority stake in Brightstar for $1.26 billion.
Then Masayoshi Son made a bigger bet on Claure himself.
In August 2014, Son chose Claure to become President and CEO of Sprint. SoftBank had paid $21.6 billion for control of Sprint in 2013. The company was losing customers and losing money. In his first fiscal year as CEO, Sprint lost $3.3 billion. The industry was skeptical. Claure had never operated a telecom network. His background was wireless distribution, not running a carrier.
He turned it around anyway. Sprint went from losing customers to adding more than 2.1 million. In fiscal 2017, it posted its highest operating income in company history and its first annual net income in 11 years.

In 2018, Son moved him again. Claure became Executive Chairman of Sprint, COO of SoftBank Group and CEO of SoftBank Group International, overseeing a portfolio that included Arm and Fortress. He kept pushing the Sprint and T-Mobile merger through a long regulatory fight, and it closed in April 2020. Today he's T-Mobile's largest independent shareholder.
At SoftBank, he also noticed a gap almost nobody was talking about: Latin American startups were getting a sliver of the venture money flowing to China and India. SoftBank launched a dedicated Latin America innovation fund to go after it.
After the George Floyd protests in 2020, Claure went to Son about doing something real. SoftBank put together a $100 million Opportunity Growth Fund for founders of color in about 24 hours.
Today Claure runs Claure Group, his own investment firm. He is Group Vice Chairman of Shein. He launched Bicycle Capital, a Latin America-focused growth fund. He owns Club Bolívar, co-owns Girona FC, and bought 10% of New York City FC. Bloomberg has estimated his net worth at about $2 billion, making him Bolivia's wealthiest person.
From a dorm-room frequent flyer business to running a carrier SoftBank paid $21.6 billion for. Built by a man who kept getting impossible jobs because the people handing them out weren't betting on his resume. They were betting on the operator.
Here's what I take from Marcelo Claure.
SoftBank didn't just buy a distribution business. It got the person running it. Then it handed him Sprint, a carrier losing billions, because it trusted the operator more than any domain expertise.
That's what I've learned across the portfolio. The partnerships that work, the clients that stay, the opportunities that open up, none of them come because of a specific credential. They come because people trust how you operate. They've seen you handle complexity, make decisions under pressure, and deliver results in one context, and they bet you can do it in another.
Nobody hires an operator for what they know about one industry. They hire an operator for how they think across all of them.

Victoire Cogevina, the CEO and co-founder of Gloria, a social media app for soccer players and fans alike, has lived in 11 cities throughout the world, and with each move, she used her fandom for soccer as a way to make new friends and find her tribe. Her dad was a Greek ambassador, and her mother Argentinian. Cogevina was born in Boston.
“Football was a vehicle to connect with the different places I lived. I made friends that way,” she said. “Football” is what the rest of the world calls “soccer.”
Cogevina founded Gloria in Miami in 2018 but soon left for San Francisco looking for a co-founder and CTO and also chasing investment dollars. Gloria – now in beta – is slated to make a soft launch this year and the full launch is scheduled for the 2022 World Cup in Qatar.
“I met my first angel investor at the World Cup and he convinced me that I would find my business partner and investors in San Francisco,” she said. Turns out he was right.
Cogevina, who recently moved back to Miami, citing it as – “the best American city for football” met Matias Castello, a fellow Argentine soccer fan and previously a product guy at Facebook. “I moved two blocks from him” and over a 6-month period, she said, she convinced him to join her as her co-founder and CTO at Gloria.
“The reason why I moved here [Miami] now is because the future of football in the U.S. is in Miami. The highest broadcasting rates come from here. Since I’m the one in charge of selling the product, I can’t be in San Francisco where football isn’t really a thing,” Cogevina said. Castello (pictured above) continues to be based in San Francisco, and the rest of the company is remote. The team of 6, which include the two co-founders and four engineers, is looking to grow. They’ll be adding more engineers to the team as well as people on the sales and marketing side.
The company plans to make money by charging a subscription rate.

While Cogevina doesn’t play soccer herself – “I play golf,” she said – for her, soccer has been more than a fun way to meet people. It’s played a large role in her career thus far. In Miami, in 2015, she and her mother founded SR All Stars, a Miami-based soccer agency representing elite LATAM professional players in the MLS. It’s the first soccer agency in the world to be started and managed solely by women, she said. Her mother still runs the agency today.
“I grew up in countries where women didn’t play soccer. So it’s great to be in the U.S. where soccer is a women’s’ sport and not a men’s’ sport,” said Cogevina, who lived largely in Europe and Latin America growing up.
As a woman who doesn’t play soccer, yet has largely worked in it, she said her mother taught her to never think of herself as a woman first, but rather just as a person.
“We forget now, because women are in fashion these days, but we forget that women weren’t allowed to play [soccer],” she said. “Whenever I brought up being a woman, she [her mom] would look at me and say ‘Why are you bringing that up? Just focus on who you are and be the best that you can be, and that’s all that matters,’” Cogevina said.
Indeed, her mother was a wealth manager who helped a lot of soccer players manage their money, and over time she found herself helping them manage their careers, too. That’s how the mother-daughter duo broke into the business of soccer.
Today, while building her app – which has received investment from Initialized Capital and Muse Capital, and has Alexis Ohanian on the board – Cogevina is also a United Nations ambassador for gender equality in soccer. Additionally, she is on the board of Women in Sports Tech (WiST), the “leading organization to drive growth opportunities for women in the fast-growing sports tech industry,” according to the organization’s website. “50% of the U.S. labor force, sports fans, and athletes are women – and yet the representation of women in sports tech is a small fraction of that,” says WiST, which aims to change that.

Cogevina never considered her gender when she had the idea for Gloria, but she remembers meeting other women who thought it was a little odd that a woman was building “the home of football online,” she said. “My mom never ever let me use my gender as an excuse to not do something,” she said.
Gloria – which I got a preview of – allows players (from amateur to professional) to upload videos of themselves playing, and it has a newly created Communities section, “which has a lot of similarities to Reddit, so it’s been amazing to have someone like Alexis guide us,” Cogevina added. Gloria recently closed a seed round for an undisclosed amount and with undisclosed investors.

# Club
## Inter Miami CF Partners with AutoNation to Drive Out Cancer; Sign Multi-Year Stadium Naming Rights and Training Top Deal
**APRIL 9, 2021**
AutoNation became the official and exclusive automotive partner of Inter Miami CF, which includes naming rights of the stadium and branding on the First Team training kits. This partnership amplifies AutoNation and Inter Miami’s commitment to driving out cancer by
leveraging the power of fútbol to do good. Starting in April 2021, Inter Miami kicked off its second campaign in Major League Soccer at the newly named DRV PNK Stadium in support of AutoNation’s DRV PNK initiative.

# Club
## Edison Azcona Becomes First Homegrown Player to Play for the First Team
**MAY 2, 2021**
In the 67th minute, Edison Azcona was subbed on for Inter Miami CF, marking the first time a Homegrown Player had represented the club at MLS level in club history. Edison Azcona was the second Homegrown signing in club history.

# Club
## Inter Miami CF Appoints Xavier Asensi as Chief Business Officer
**APRIL 8, 2021**
Inter Miami CF announced that it appointed Xavier Asensi as Chief Business Officer. Asensi, 39,joins Inter Miami after 10 years with FC Barcelona, where he most recently served as Chief Commercial Officer and was a member of the FC Barcelona Executive Board. “Xavi brings a proven record of success at one of the world’s greatest clubs,” said Inter Miami CF Managing Owner Jorge Mas. “His vision will further drive the growth of our Club and support our local and commercial partnerships.” “I am grateful for the trust and support Jorge Mas and David Beckham have given me, and I am very motivated and excited to begin this new journey in South Florida. I am a huge fan of the United States and I believe that there is no better time to be part of the soccer industry in this country alongside a young organization with a world of opportunities ahead,” said newly appointed Chief Business Officer Xavier Asensi. “I’ve been very impressed with what I’ve seen so far and look forward to working with the team to establish a clear direction and strategy to achieve our goals.”

# Club
## Inter Miami CF Launch Primeblue Jersey Underwater in the Cayman Islands
**June 8, 2021**
Plastic pollution is a significant issue for the world, especially with regards to the ocean. The issue must be at the forefront of mind at all times to not only ensure continued awareness of, but also to remember that it is up to us to be part of the solution. With this in mind, Inter Miami launched its adidas Primeblue jersey made with Parley Ocean Plastic in collaboration with Major League Soccer ahead of World Oceans Day on June 8, becoming the first team in history to ever launch a jersey fully underwater.

# Club
## Inter Miami CF Opens DRV PNK Stadium to a Sell-Out Crowd
**JUNE 25, 2021**
On a Friday night vs. local rival Orlando City SC, DRV PNK Stadium was allowed to function at full capacity due to COVID-19 restrictions being lifted, and it was host to the first sell-out in club history.

# Club
## Inter Miami CF Inks Primary Jersey Sponsor Deal With Leading Crypto Finance Firm XBTO
**Wednesday, Sept. 15**
Inter Miami unveiled XBTO, a prominent, global cryptofinance firm, as the first-ever Primary Jersey Sponsor for South Florida’s Major League Soccer (MLS) Club. The deal between Inter Miami and XBTO marks the first cryptofinance partnership in MLS.
Inter Miami players, Club co-owners and prominent members of the Miami tech community participated in the special event to discuss the partnership and the many benefits of the booming crypto industry.

# Club
## Inter Miami Owners Mas Brothers, Beckham Increase Ownership Stake in the Club
**SEPTEMBER 17, 2021**
Inter Miami CF announced Jorge and Jose Mas and David Beckham finalized the buyout of Marcelo Claure and Masayoshi Son. In addition, Ares Management (“Ares”) joined the Club as a preferred equity investor through funds managed by its Credit Group.

# Club
## First-Ever Pink Kit, “The Heartbeat Kit” Unveiled
**FEBRUARY 19, 2022**
Inspired by and designed for the fans of Inter Miami CF – the true heartbeat of the team – the kit is the first all-pink jersey in club history. On the cuff of the jersey sleeves and on the jock tag, the fans are represented by an M-shaped line embossed into the fabric. Illustrating how the fans are the heartbeat of the club, the M is designed like a line from an electrocardiogram (EKG). In an additional design touch reflecting the true spirit between the club and its supporters, there is an inscription on the back of the neck of jersey that reads “Libertad Para Soñar” (Freedom to Dream). The design and font utilized are from a tattoo of IMCF Owner and President of Soccer
Operations David Beckham. The words were originally scripted in the handwriting of Beckham’s close friend – the global superstar singer, songwriter, recording executive and actor Marc Anthony.

# Club
## Inter Miami CF II Announced to Join MLS NEXT PRO League
**MARCH 22, 2022**
Fort Lauderdale CF rebranded to Inter Miami CF II, and joined the MLS’ new development league, MLS NEXT PRO, where they continue to be the bridge between the Club’s Academy and the MLS First Team.

# Club
## The City of Miami Commissions Vote ‘Yes’ on Miami Freedom Park Project
**APRIL 28, 2022**
The City of Miami Commission made the people of Miami’s dream a reality, by voting to approve Miami Freedom Park. Miami Freedom Park will contain a 27,000-seat stadium, 750 hotel rooms, commercial and office space, community fields and the single largest public park in the city of Miami with over 58 acres of freely accessible, clean park land.

# Club
## 2022 adidas Primeblue Jersey Underwater Unveiled with Marine Life to Highlight the Beauty of a Healthy Ocean
**MAY 26, 2022**
Inter Miami CF returned to the Cayman Islands to build on its 2021 campaign to capture the launch of its second Primeblue jersey “Everyone at the club was excited to work with Jason, Coral, adidas and MLS again on such an important initiative as reducing plastic pollution in the Ocean. This year, we really wanted to find a way to highlight that when the Oceans are clear of plastic, marine life will repopulate and ultimately flourish, which is critical to a healthy ecosystem.” — Inter Miami CF SVP, Brand and Marketing, Mike Ridley

# Club
## Apple and Major League Soccer to Present All MLS Matches Around the World for 10 Years, Beginning in 2023
**JUNE 14, 2022**
Apple and Major League Soccer announced that the Apple TV app will be the exclusive destination to watch every single live MLS match beginning in 2023. This partnership is a historic first for a major professional sports league and will allow fans around the world to watch all MLS, Leagues Cup, and select MLS NEXT Pro and MLS NEXT matches in one place -- without any local broadcast blackouts or the need for a traditional pay TV bundle.

# Club
## Inter Miami CF Hosts FC Barcelona for a Summer Friendly to a Sold Out DRV PNK Stadium
**JULY 19, 2022**
For the first time in Club history, we opened our doors for an International friendly during the season, by playing against Spanish Giants FC Barcelona at DRV PNK Stadium. FC Barcelona trained at facilities for 3 days and played against our first team in the largest crowd in DRV PNK Stadium history.

# Club
## Inter Miami CF Foundation Unveiled with Focus on Harnessing the Power of Fútbol to Do Good
**AUGUST 17, 2022**
Inter Miami CF announced its 501©3 community-driven nonprofit arm, the Inter Miami CF Foundation on National Nonprofit Day. “Our goal through the Inter Miami CF Foundation is to harness the power of fútbol to break down barriers on and off the pitch, ensuring that youth across South Florida have the tools and support they need,” said Adriana Sandoval, Inter Miami CF Director of Community Engagement & Foundation.

# Club
## Inter Miami CF Partners with Florida Blue; Signs Major, Multi-Year Partnership and Secures Naming Rights of Training Center
**SEPTEMBER 12, 2022**
Inter Miami CF announced a major, multi-year partnership with Florida Blue. The state’s Blue Cross Blue Shield plan joins Inter Miami as the Club’s Official Community Partner and secures the naming rights for the state-of-the-art, $60-million training facility in Fort Lauderdale, now the Florida Blue Training Center. Continuing a trend of aligning with local, like-minded brands, this relationship is rooted in a desire to strengthen the local community and further Inter Miami’s mission to harness the power of fútbol to do good.

# Club
## Inter Miami CF Clinches Playoffs for Second Time in Three Seasons
**OCTOBER 5, 2022**
Inter Miami qualified for the MLS Playoffs for the second time in three seasons by beating local rival Orlando City SC at DRV PNK Stadium 4-1, the largest margin of victory in the 2022 season. Leo Campana scored the fastest goal in Inter Miami CF History, scoring after 35 seconds.

# Club
## Adidas One Planet Jersey Unveiled with Great Hammerhead Shark
**APRIL 18, 2023**
For the third edition of the campaign, Coral Cay and Cayman Jason went to the Bahamas to release this year’s One Planet Jersey underwater next to a Great Hammerhead Shark to promote responsible plastic use and the positive impact it can have on our ocean habitat. "The One Planet initiative is special to our Club. This year we wanted to complete the trilogy with Jason and Coral alongside the ocean’s apex predator as a symbol of a healthy ecosystem, which is the ultimate goal of One Planet. We’re grateful for adidas and MLS for continuing to work with us towards that goal,” said Mike Ridley, Inter Miami CF SVP of Brand and Marketing."

# Club
## Four Homegrown Players Start for the First Team
**JUNE 10, 2023**
Away at New England Revolution, Inter Miami made history for starting four Homegrown products in one match for the first time. Noah Allen, Ian Fray, David Ruiz and Benjamin Cremaschi were all included all of which played in the Inter Miami Academy and for the Second Team.

# Club
## Gerard ‘Tata’ Martino announced as Head Coach
**JUNE 28, 2023**
Inter Miami CF announced that its named the MLS Cup winner, two-time manager at a FIFA World Cup, three-time Conmebol Copa América finalist, Concacaf Gold Cup winner and former FC Barcelona and Argentina National Team manager Gerardo ‘Tata’ Martino as head coach. “I’m very excited to join a big club like Inter Miami and I know together we can accomplish many great things,” said incoming Inter Miami CF head coach Martino. “The Club has the necessary infrastructure to be a major competitor in the region and I believe that with everyone’s hard work and commitment we can get there.”

# Club
## Inter Miami CF Signs Seven-Time Ballon d'Or Winner, World Cup Champion, Lionel Messi
**JULY 15, 2023**
Inter Miami CF today announced the signing of seven-time Ballon d’Or winner and World Cup Champion, Lionel Messi.
“I am honored to welcome Leo Messi and his family to their new home,” said Inter Miami CF Managing Owner, Jorge Mas. “In 2018, we made a promise to build an ambitious club that would attract the world’s elite players. A club that would transform the global view of fútbol in the United States and ensure that wherever fútbol is discussed, your Inter Miami is part of the conversation. A heartfelt thank you to our fans that never stopped believing. Together we will continue to turn dreams into reality.”

# Club
## Inter Miami CF Signs Legendary Midfielder Sergio Busquets
**JULY 16, 2023**
Inter Miami CF announced today that it has signed World Cup champion and nine-time LaLiga winner Sergio Busquets.
“This is a special and exciting opportunity that I’m very excited to take. I’m looking forward to this next step in my career with Inter Miami,” said Busquets. “I was impressed by the Club when I came with Barcelona last year and now I’m happy and ready to represent the Club myself. I can’t wait to help bring the success that this ambitious Club strives for.”

# Club
## Inter Miami CF Signs Spanish International Defender Jordi Alba
**JULY 20, 2023**
Inter Miami CF announced today that it has signed Spanish national team defender and UEFA Euro winner, UEFA Champions League winner, UEFA Nations League winner, and six-time LaLiga winner Jordi Alba to a contract through the 2024 Major League Soccer (MLS) season, with a Club option for 2025.
“Jordi is an accomplished, dynamic and experienced player that we’re excited to acquire to continue bolstering our squad. He has proven for over a decade that he is one of the best fullbacks in the sport due to both his defensive solidity and capacity to contribute in the attack. We know that he’ll help Inter Miami achieve the Club’s objectives this season and beyond,” said Chief Soccer Director and Sporting Director Chris Henderson.

# Club
## Inter Miami Crowned Inaugural Leagues Cup Champions
**AUGUST 19, 2023**
Inter Miami CF achieved another major milestone for the Club on Saturday night, making history by defeating Nashville SC at GEODIS Park in a dramatic penalty shootout to win the 2023 Leagues Cup title and clinch the First Team’s first official piece of silverware. The match ended 1-1 in regulation and featured a stellar performance in between the sticks from Man of the Match Drake Callender and a stunner from Lionel Messi to open the scoring in the first half.
Individually, two Inter Miami players also enjoyed the historic night in Tennessee, with Messi becoming the player with most trophies in the history of the sport with 44 and collecting Leagues Cup Best Player and Top Scorer awards. Goalkeeper Callender, meanwhile, earned Man of the Match honors for his stellar performance in the final as well as the Leagues Cup Best Goalkeeper award.

# Club
## Inter Miami CF Signs Iconic Striker Luis Suárez
**DECEMBER 22, 2023**
Inter Miami CF announced that it has signed UEFA Champions League, FIFA Club World Cup, and Conmebol Copa América winner and five-time LaLiga champion Luis Suárez to a contract running through the 2024 Major League Soccer (MLS) season. The iconic Uruguayan striker will join the team ahead of the 2024 MLS season after being named the Best Player and Best Striker in the Brazilian league thanks to his 26 goals and 17 assists over 53 appearances, and leading Grêmio to win the Campeonato Gaúcho and Recopa Gaúcha.

# Club
## Club’s Third Kit Unveiled as Part of Special Throwback-Themed Archive Collection
**JULY 16, 2024**
Inter Miami CF and adidas announced the official unveiling of the Club’s highly-anticipated third kit. Tapping on 80’s nostalgia, Inter Miami’s archive kit leans heavily on the vibrancy of vintage Miami style. The collection consists of a jersey, jacket, Gazelle, and Samba shoes, featuring bold and progressive designs.

# Club
## Inter Miami CF Appoints Javier Mascherano as Head Coach
**NOVEMBER 26, 2024**
Inter Miami CF announced that it has named Argentina and FC Barcelona legend Javier Mascherano as its head coach, signing him to a contract through the 2027 Major League Soccer (MLS) season. The Argentine joins following a period as the head coach of the Argentina U-20 and Olympic national teams, and will assume coaching responsibilities at Inter Miami upon the receipt of his work documentation.

* * *
April 5, 2021
The University of Miami athletics department today announced that it has selected Legends, a premium experiences company, to oversee marketing partnerships and rights for the Miami Hurricanes.
Through this new partnership, Legends will collaborate with Miami to develop a comprehensive sponsorship strategy and establish meaningful, integrated partnerships that connect brands and corporate partners with the Hurricanes’ passionate fanbase. Legends will bring new partnerships to the university that will celebrate Miami’s rich athletic traditions, its talented student-athletes, and the forward-thinking leadership and innovation of the athletics program.
“We are excited to partner with Legends on our corporate sponsorships and marketing rights,” said Blake James, University of Miami’s Director of Athletics. “Legends works with some of the most recognized brands in sports and we are confident that they can help us leverage both our iconic brand and location in one of the world’s most vibrant cities to drive value for our department, our fans and our partners.We are thrilled to see what the partnership will bring in the years to come.”
Legends will also lead a thorough analysis and valuation of sponsorship rights and introduce its proprietary, data and analytics-driven business intelligence platform, to help identify new opportunities and provide greater insights into Hurricanes fans’ behaviors and interests.
“Miami has built one of the nation’s great athletics programs, and we see tremendous value in creating a customized sponsorship approach that celebrates the university’s unique history and rich athletics traditions, and particularity of the Miami market,” said Mike Behan, Legends Vice President, Collegiate Partnerships. “Our team at Legends will draw upon our vast experience working with the most creative and innovative brands across sports, media, and entertainment, to help expand the incredible opportunities available through this partnership.”
Legends, a global leader in sports and entertainment, was founded by the New York Yankees and Dallas Cowboys. Legends leads significant sponsorship sales efforts across professional and collegiate sports including for the Los Angeles Rams and Los Angeles Chargers, Las Vegas Raiders, Orlando Magic, University of Notre Dame, Georgia Tech, and LA28.
Legends will open a sales and engagement center in South Miami.

I am a huge fan of the United States and I believe that there is no better time to be part of the soccer industry in this country alongside a young organization with a world of opportunities ahead,” said newly appointed Chief Business Officer Xavier Asensi. “I’ve been very impressed with what I’ve seen so far and look forward to working with the team to establish a clear direction and strategy to achieve our goals.”

# Club
## Inter Miami CF Launch Primeblue Jersey Underwater in the Cayman Islands
**June 8, 2021**
Plastic pollution is a significant issue for the world, especially with regards to the ocean. The issue must be at the forefront of mind at all times to not only ensure continued awareness of, but also to remember that it is up to us to be part of the solution. With this in mind, Inter Miami launched its adidas Primeblue jersey made with Parley Ocean Plastic in collaboration with Major League Soccer ahead of World Oceans Day on June 8, becoming the first team in history to ever launch a jersey fully underwater.

**JUNE 25, 2021**

## Inter Miami CF Inks Primary Jersey Sponsor Deal With Leading Crypto Finance Firm XBTO
**Wednesday, Sept. 15**
Inter Miami unveiled XBTO, a prominent, global cryptofinance firm, as the first-ever Primary Jersey Sponsor for South Florida’s Major League Soccer (MLS) Club. The deal between Inter Miami and XBTO marks the first cryptofinance partnership in MLS.

## Inter Miami Owners Mas Brothers, Beckham Increase Ownership Stake in the Club
**SEPTEMBER 17, 2021**
Inter Miami CF announced Jorge and Jose Mas and David Beckham finalized the buyout of Marcelo Claure and Masayoshi Son. In addition, Ares Management (“Ares”) joined the Club as a preferred equity investor through funds managed by its Credit Group.

# Club
## First-Ever Pink Kit, “The Heartbeat Kit” Unveiled
**FEBRUARY 19, 2022**
Inspired by and designed for the fans of Inter Miami CF – the true heartbeat of the team – the kit is the first all-pink jersey in club history. On the cuff of the jersey sleeves and on the jock tag, the fans are represented by an M-shaped line embossed into the fabric. Illustrating how the fans are the heartbeat of the club, the M is designed like a line from an electrocardiogram (EKG). In an additional design touch reflecting the true spirit between the club and its supporters, there is an inscription on the back of the neck of jersey that reads “Libertad Para Soñar” (Freedom to Dream). The design and font utilized are from a tattoo of IMCF Owner and President of Soccer
Operations David Beckham. The words were originally scripted in the handwriting of Beckham’s close friend – the global superstar singer, songwriter, recording executive and actor Marc Anthony.

**AUGUST 17, 2022**

**SEPTEMBER 12, 2022**
Inter Miami CF announced a major, multi-year partnership with Florida Blue. The state’s Blue Cross Blue Shield plan joins Inter Miami as the Club’s Official Community Partner and secures the naming rights for the state-of-the-art, $60-million training facility in Fort Lauderdale, now the Florida Blue Training Center. **OCTOBER 5, 2022**

**APRIL 18, 2023**

Inter Miami CF today announced the signing of seven-time Ballon d’Or winner and World Cup Champion, Lionel Messi.

# Club
## Inter Miami CF Signs Spanish International Defender Jordi Alba
**JULY 20, 2023**
Inter Miami CF announced today that it has signed Spanish national team defender and UEFA Euro winner, UEFA Champions League winner, UEFA Nations League winner, and six-time LaLiga winner Jordi Alba to a contract through the 2024 Major League Soccer (MLS) season, with a Club option for 2025.
“Jordi is an accomplished, dynamic and experienced player that we’re excited to acquire to continue bolstering our squad. We know that he’ll help Inter Miami achieve the Club’s objectives this season and beyond,” said Chief Soccer Director and Sporting Director Chris Henderson.

# Club
## Inter Miami Crowned Inaugural Leagues Cup Champions
**AUGUST 19, 2023**
Inter Miami CF achieved another major milestone for the Club on Saturday night, making history by defeating Nashville SC at GEODIS Park in a dramatic penalty shootout to win the 2023 Leagues Cup title and clinch the First Team’s first official piece of silverware. The match ended 1-1 in regulation and featured a stellar performance in between the sticks from Man of the Match Drake Callender and a stunner from Lionel Messi to open the scoring in the first half.
Individually, two Inter Miami players also enjoyed the historic night in Tennessee, with Messi becoming the player with most trophies in the history of the sport with 44 and collecting Leagues Cup Best Player and Top Scorer awards. Goalkeeper Callender, meanwhile, earned Man of the Match honors for his stellar performance in the final as well as the Leagues Cup Best Goalkeeper award.

**DECEMBER 22, 2023**
Inter Miami CF announced that it has signed UEFA Champions League, FIFA Club World Cup, and Conmebol Copa América winner and five-time LaLiga champion Luis Suárez to a contract running through the 2024 Major League Soccer (MLS) season. ## First-Ever Pink Kit, “The Heartbeat Kit” Unveiled
**FEBRUARY 19, 2022**
Inspired by and designed for the fans of Inter Miami CF – the true heartbeat of the team – the kit is the first all-pink jersey in club history. On the cuff of the jersey sleeves and on the jock tag, the fans are represented by an M-shaped line embossed into the fabric. Illustrating how the fans are the heartbeat of the club, the M is designed like a line from an electrocardiogram (EKG). In an additional design touch reflecting the true spirit between the club and its supporters, there is an inscription on the back of the neck of jersey that reads “Libertad Para Soñar” (Freedom to Dream). The design and font utilized are from a tattoo of IMCF Owner and President of Soccer
Operations David Beckham. The words were originally scripted in the handwriting of Beckham’s close friend – the global superstar singer, songwriter, recording executive and actor Marc Anthony.

# Club
## Inter Miami CF II Announced to Join MLS NEXT PRO League
**MARCH 22, 2022**
Fort Lauderdale CF rebranded to Inter Miami CF II, and joined the MLS’ new development league, MLS NEXT PRO, where they continue to be the bridge between the Club’s Academy and the MLS First Team.

# Club
## The City of Miami Commissions Vote ‘Yes’ on Miami Freedom Park Project
**APRIL 28, 2022**
The City of Miami Commission made the people of Miami’s dream a reality, by voting to approve Miami Freedom Park. Miami Freedom Park will contain a 27,000-seat stadium, 750 hotel rooms, commercial and office space, community fields and the single largest public park in the city of Miami with over 58 acres of freely accessible, clean park land.

# Club
## 2022 adidas Primeblue Jersey Underwater Unveiled with Marine Life to Highlight the Beauty of a Healthy Ocean
**MAY 26, 2022**
Inter Miami CF returned to the Cayman Islands to build on its 2021 campaign to capture the launch of its second Primeblue jersey “Everyone at the club was excited to work with Jason, Coral, adidas and MLS again on such an important initiative as reducing plastic pollution in the Ocean. This year, we really wanted to find a way to highlight that when the Oceans are clear of plastic, marine life will repopulate and ultimately flourish, which is critical to a healthy ecosystem.” — Inter Miami CF SVP, Brand and Marketing, Mike Ridley

# Club
## Apple and Major League Soccer to Present All MLS Matches Around the World for 10 Years, Beginning in 2023
**JUNE 14, 2022**
Apple and Major League Soccer announced that the Apple TV app will be the exclusive destination to watch every single live MLS match beginning in 2023. This partnership is a historic first for a major professional sports league and will allow fans around the world to watch all MLS, Leagues Cup, and select MLS NEXT Pro and MLS NEXT matches in one place -- without any local broadcast blackouts or the need for a traditional pay TV bundle.

# Club
## Inter Miami CF Hosts FC Barcelona for a Summer Friendly to a Sold Out DRV PNK Stadium
**JULY 19, 2022**
For the first time in Club history, we opened our doors for an International friendly during the season, by playing against Spanish Giants FC Barcelona at DRV PNK Stadium. FC Barcelona trained at facilities for 3 days and played against our first team in the largest crowd in DRV PNK Stadium history.

# Club
## Inter Miami CF Foundation Unveiled with Focus on Harnessing the Power of Fútbol to Do Good
**AUGUST 17, 2022**
Inter Miami CF announced its 501©3 community-driven nonprofit arm, the Inter Miami CF Foundation on National Nonprofit Day. “Our goal through the Inter Miami CF Foundation is to harness the power of fútbol to break down barriers on and off the pitch, ensuring that youth across South Florida have the tools and support they need,” said Adriana Sandoval, Inter Miami CF Director of Community Engagement & Foundation.

# Club
## Inter Miami CF Partners with Florida Blue; Signs Major, Multi-Year Partnership and Secures Naming Rights of Training Center
**SEPTEMBER 12, 2022**
Inter Miami CF announced a major, multi-year partnership with Florida Blue. The state’s Blue Cross Blue Shield plan joins Inter Miami as the Club’s Official Community Partner and secures the naming rights for the state-of-the-art, $60-million training facility in Fort Lauderdale, now the Florida Blue Training Center. Continuing a trend of aligning with local, like-minded brands, this relationship is rooted in a desire to strengthen the local community and further Inter Miami’s mission to harness the power of fútbol to do good.

# Club
## Inter Miami CF Clinches Playoffs for Second Time in Three Seasons
**OCTOBER 5, 2022**
Inter Miami qualified for the MLS Playoffs for the second time in three seasons by beating local rival Orlando City SC at DRV PNK Stadium 4-1, the largest margin of victory in the 2022 season. Leo Campana scored the fastest goal in Inter Miami CF History, scoring after 35 seconds.

# Club
## Adidas One Planet Jersey Unveiled with Great Hammerhead Shark
**APRIL 18, 2023**
For the third edition of the campaign, Coral Cay and Cayman Jason went to the Bahamas to release this year’s One Planet Jersey underwater next to a Great Hammerhead Shark to promote responsible plastic use and the positive impact it can have on our ocean habitat. "The One Planet initiative is special to our Club. This year we wanted to complete the trilogy with Jason and Coral alongside the ocean’s apex predator as a symbol of a healthy ecosystem, which is the ultimate goal of One Planet. We’re grateful for adidas and MLS for continuing to work with us towards that goal,” said Mike Ridley, Inter Miami CF SVP of Brand and Marketing."

# Club
## Four Homegrown Players Start for the First Team
**JUNE 10, 2023**
Away at New England Revolution, Inter Miami made history for starting four Homegrown products in one match for the first time. Noah Allen, Ian Fray, David Ruiz and Benjamin Cremaschi were all included all of which played in the Inter Miami Academy and for the Second Team.

# Club
## Gerard ‘Tata’ Martino announced as Head Coach
**JUNE 28, 2023**
Inter Miami CF announced that its named the MLS Cup winner, two-time manager at a FIFA World Cup, three-time Conmebol Copa América finalist, Concacaf Gold Cup winner and former FC Barcelona and Argentina National Team manager Gerardo ‘Tata’ Martino as head coach. “I’m very excited to join a big club like Inter Miami and I know together we can accomplish many great things,” said incoming Inter Miami CF head coach Martino. “The Club has the necessary infrastructure to be a major competitor in the region and I believe that with everyone’s hard work and commitment we can get there.”

# Club
## Inter Miami CF Signs Seven-Time Ballon d'Or Winner, World Cup Champion, Lionel Messi
**JULY 15, 2023**
Inter Miami CF today announced the signing of seven-time Ballon d’Or winner and World Cup Champion, Lionel Messi.
“I am honored to welcome Leo Messi and his family to their new home,” said Inter Miami CF Managing Owner, Jorge Mas. “In 2018, we made a promise to build an ambitious club that would attract the world’s elite players. A club that would transform the global view of fútbol in the United States and ensure that wherever fútbol is discussed, your Inter Miami is part of the conversation. A heartfelt thank you to our fans that never stopped believing. Together we will continue to turn dreams into reality.”

# Club
## Inter Miami CF Signs Legendary Midfielder Sergio Busquets
**JULY 16, 2023**
Inter Miami CF announced today that it has signed World Cup champion and nine-time LaLiga winner Sergio Busquets.
“This is a special and exciting opportunity that I’m very excited to take. I’m looking forward to this next step in my career with Inter Miami,” said Busquets. “I was impressed by the Club when I came with Barcelona last year and now I’m happy and ready to represent the Club myself. I can’t wait to help bring the success that this ambitious Club strives for.”

# Club
## Inter Miami CF Signs Spanish International Defender Jordi Alba
**JULY 20, 2023**
Inter Miami CF announced today that it has signed Spanish national team defender and UEFA Euro winner, UEFA Champions League winner, UEFA Nations League winner, and six-time LaLiga winner Jordi Alba to a contract through the 2024 Major League Soccer (MLS) season, with a Club option for 2025.
“Jordi is an accomplished, dynamic and experienced player that we’re excited to acquire to continue bolstering our squad. He has proven for over a decade that he is one of the best fullbacks in the sport due to both his defensive solidity and capacity to contribute in the attack. We know that he’ll help Inter Miami achieve the Club’s objectives this season and beyond,” said Chief Soccer Director and Sporting Director Chris Henderson.

# Club
## Inter Miami Crowned Inaugural Leagues Cup Champions
**AUGUST 19, 2023**
Inter Miami CF achieved another major milestone for the Club on Saturday night, making history by defeating Nashville SC at GEODIS Park in a dramatic penalty shootout to win the 2023 Leagues Cup title and clinch the First Team’s first official piece of silverware. The match ended 1-1 in regulation and featured a stellar performance in between the sticks from Man of the Match Drake Callender and a stunner from Lionel Messi to open the scoring in the first half.
Individually, two Inter Miami players also enjoyed the historic night in Tennessee, with Messi becoming the player with most trophies in the history of the sport with 44 and collecting Leagues Cup Best Player and Top Scorer awards. Goalkeeper Callender, meanwhile, earned Man of the Match honors for his stellar performance in the final as well as the Leagues Cup Best Goalkeeper award.

# Club
## Inter Miami CF Signs Iconic Striker Luis Suárez
**DECEMBER 22, 2023**
Inter Miami CF announced that it has signed UEFA Champions League, FIFA Club World Cup, and Conmebol Copa América winner and five-time LaLiga champion Luis Suárez to a contract running through the 2024 Major League Soccer (MLS) season. The iconic Uruguayan striker will join the team ahead of the 2024 MLS season after being named the Best Player and Best Striker in the Brazilian league thanks to his 26 goals and 17 assists over 53 appearances, and leading Grêmio to win the Campeonato Gaúcho and Recopa Gaúcha.

# Club
## Club’s Third Kit Unveiled as Part of Special Throwback-Themed Archive Collection
**JULY 16, 2024**
Inter Miami CF and adidas announced the official unveiling of the Club’s highly-anticipated third kit. Tapping on 80’s nostalgia, Inter Miami’s archive kit leans heavily on the vibrancy of vintage Miami style. The collection consists of a jersey, jacket, Gazelle, and Samba shoes, featuring bold and progressive designs.

# Club
## Inter Miami CF Appoints Javier Mascherano as Head Coach
**NOVEMBER 26, 2024**
Inter Miami CF announced that it has named Argentina and FC Barcelona legend Javier Mascherano as its head coach, signing him to a contract through the 2027 Major League Soccer (MLS) season. The Argentine joins following a period as the head coach of the Argentina U-20 and Olympic national teams, and will assume coaching responsibilities at Inter Miami upon the receipt of his work documentation.

Title: Top Gatorade Sponsored Athletes and Their Endorsement Deals (May 2026)
Chunks: 0,1,2,3,4,5,6,7,8
When you search for Gatorade sponsored athletes 2026, you will not find a single, tidy public master roster. Gatorade and PepsiCo announce athletes in launches, campaigns, and NIL reporting, so any “full list” is stitched from official releases plus trade press.
Because there is no one public “master roster,” the cleanest documented slice of who Gatorade is highlighting _right now_ is what PepsiCo and Gatorade attach to a given launch. Everything else sits in campaign-specific announcements, legacy relationships, or NIL reporting—and “active today” may differ from “featured in one ad.”

### 2026 “Body of Science” roster (women, named by Gatorade/PepsiCo)
For the 2026 “Body of Science” launch, Gatorade and PepsiCo explicitly named these athletes as part of the roster:
*   A’ja Wilson  
*   Sydney McLaughlin-Levrone  
*   Lisa Billard  
*   Paige Bueckers  
*   Caitlin Clark  
*   Diana Flores  
*   Candace Parker  
*   Mallory Swanson  
*   JuJu Watkins  
*   Sophia Wilson
That is a defined, citeable set; it is not the same as “everyone Gatorade has ever paid or might still use in archival footage.”

### College basketball and NIL (reporting-backed sequence)
Gatorade’s NCAA basketball NIL story, as reported in the trades, follows a clear order:
*   **Paige Bueckers** — described as the first college athlete to sign with Gatorade.  
*   **Caitlin Clark** — signed while at Iowa; the brand relationship continued after she turned pro.  
*   **JuJu Watkins** — joined the elite roster as the **third** NCAA women’s basketball NIL signing after Bueckers and Clark.  
*   **Cooper Flagg** — the **first men’s** NCAA basketball player to sign with Gatorade.
Those details matter for anyone comparing Gatorade to volume-first college strategies: the brand often picks nationally known names early, not a long tail of roster filler. Partnerships still imply product usage, content duties, and category exclusivity clauses where negotiated.

### Legacy and global: “GOAT Camp”
Gatorade has grouped **Michael Jordan**, **Serena Williams**, **Lionel Messi**, and **Usain Bolt** in its global “GOAT Camp” push—a useful anchor for “all-time face of the brand” talent even when day-to-day campaign rotation changes.

### Other notable past or reported names (not a current roster)
Trade and campaign coverage have also tied Gatorade to names such as **Mia Hamm**, **Abby Wambach**, **Jayson Tatum**, **Karl-Anthony Towns**, **Peyton Manning**, **Eli Manning**, **Dwyane Wade**, **Derek Jeter**, and **J.J. Watt**, alongside figures already listed above (e.g. **Candace Parker**). Treat these as **legacy, regional, or campaign-specific** unless a fresh release says otherwise—exactly because Gatorade does not publish one consolidated list.
College athlete deals more broadly took off after 2021 NIL rules, giving brands access to student-athletes before the pro draft. Gatorade’s public pattern has skewed toward hoops and other high-visibility sports when it wants headline density, not necessarily toward the longest possible tally of signings.

## Understanding Gatorade Player of the Year Awards
The Gatorade Player of the Year program recognizes elite high school athletes across 12 sports, functioning as both an awards system and a talent identification pipeline. Winners receive national recognition that often precedes professional success.
Each year, Gatorade selects 610 State Players of the Year across sports including football, basketball, baseball, soccer, and volleyball. From that pool, 12 National Players of the Year get chosen, one per sport. Selection criteria weigh athletic performance, academic achievement, and community involvement.
Past winners include Peyton Manning, LeBron James, Jayson Tatum, and Paige Bueckers. These athletes earned the recognition before college recruitment, giving them visibility when it matters most for scholarship offers. College coaches track Gatorade Player of the Year recipients as indicators of future performance and potential NIL value.

## Gatorade's NIL Deals With College Athletes
Gatorade entered college NIL partnerships by targeting athletes with existing national profiles: **Paige Bueckers** and **Caitlin Clark** before **JuJu Watkins** (third women’s NCAA basketball NIL in that sequence, as typically reported). When you search for Gatorade sponsored athletes 2026, you will not find a single, tidy public master roster. Gatorade and PepsiCo announce athletes in launches, campaigns, and NIL reporting, so any “full list” is stitched from official releases plus trade press.
Because there is no one public “master roster,” the cleanest documented slice of who Gatorade is highlighting _right now_ is what PepsiCo and Gatorade attach to a given launch. Everything else sits in campaign-specific announcements, legacy relationships, or NIL reporting—and “active today” may differ from “featured in one ad.”

### 2026 “Body of Science” roster (women, named by Gatorade/PepsiCo)
For the 2026 “Body of Science” launch, Gatorade and PepsiCo explicitly named these athletes as part of the roster:
*   A’ja Wilson  
*   Sydney McLaughlin-Levrone  
*   Lisa Billard  
*   Paige Bueckers  
*   Caitlin Clark
